correctness.rationale: The proof first reduces the power-zero condition to avoidance of t cyclically consecutive domain sites in each rotation cycle. Weighted transition-trace enumeration and Euler-totient order-fiber counts give the exact polynomial, with one-zero correction. The high-index law follows from the fact that every proper divisor of n is <=n/2 and the uniqueness of a long cyclic one-run. The logarithmic limit follows from explicit uniform upper and lower tail inequalities even for composite n. Actual partial-map and independent polynomial-matrix enumeration agree coefficientwise for n=2,...,10, and the all-n claim is proved separately.

originality.rationale: Two inspected relevant primary full texts and targeted literature and published-record searches did not establish a matching or stronger statement. Fernandes constructs this precise monoid and determines its size and presentations, whereas the new claim refines nilpotent elements jointly by domain rank and first zero power and gives a totient-dependent exact upper tail. Elliott–Levine–Mitchell count isomorphism types rather than elements by power threshold. OEIS A261764 is for all partial permutations, so cannot determine restriction-specific counts; even its n=4 nilpotent total (73) differs from the present cyclic count (37). Previously recorded chain partial-isometry formulas do not entail the cyclic order-divisor sum. Remaining priority risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Search and retrieved publications cannot establish global priority; an unindexed cyclic partial-rotation run enumeration may already exist.
General forbidden-run transfer matrix methods are classical; this is claimed as a new application and sharp arithmetic refinement, not a new automata identity.
A closely related rank/index enumeration for order-preserving partial isometries of chains exists but covers a different semigroup and has no circular order-divisor strata.

value.rationale: Least zero power and rank are natural semigroup invariants. For a well-studied rank-two cyclic inverse monoid, the complete bivariate spectrum is not recoverable from the known cardinality, generator rank or unrestricted inverse-monoid tables. Its unusual exact upper tail is governed by Euler totient and a binomial rank law for all n, while logarithmic typical behavior separates bulk and exceptional elements. These give a natural complete classification and an arithmetic structural consequence rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
